purpose: Country-specific agricultural evidence inventory for later validation; not a production calculator profile.

sections.topic: government-led crop and food supply assessment
sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Sudan Country Brief, drawing on 2025 Crop and Food Supply Assessment Mission
sections.reference_date: GIEWS reference date 24 September 2026; FAO CFSAM announcement 26 April 2026

observations.item: National cereal production (sorghum, millet and wheat)
observations.finding: About 22 percent below 2024 and 19 percent below the previous five-year average.
FAO reported sorghum production decreased by about 25 percent compared with 2024.
FAO reported millet production remained 46 percent below the five-year average.
About 12 percent below the 2024 level.

caveats: National aggregate output is not a crop-specific state-level yield or farm-level production figure.
Extract original CFSAM tables for crop area, harvested area, production, yield and state coverage before calculator use.
Retain separate production-year, marketing-year and harvest-season labels.

observations.finding: Planting of 2026 cereal crops for harvest from November 2026 was completed by mid-August.
Below-average cumulative rainfall over most cropping areas affected germination and crop establishment; significant deficits occurred in southeastern key cropping areas.
Seasonal rainfall in Sennar was about 20 percent below average.
Seasonal rainfall in Gedaref was about 30 percent below average.

observations.value: up to 55% in Sennar; up to 70% in Gedaref
observations.finding: Severe drought conditions affected substantial shares of cropland in these two major sorghum-producing states.

caveats: The 2026 harvest had not been completed at the reference date; do not treat the outlook as final production.
Sennar and Gedaref together normally account for about one quarter of national sorghum output, but this share is not a current-year crop forecast.
Rainfall, conflict and input access vary by state and district.

sections.topic: agroecological production systems and crop portfolio

observations.finding: Agriculture provides food and income to nearly 65 percent of the population.
Irrigated agriculture includes the Al Jazirah Scheme, described by FAO as covering approximately one million hectares.
Semi-mechanized rainfed agriculture is concentrated in a belt of about 6.7 million hectares.
Traditional rainfed agriculture spans about 9 million hectares and engages most farmers.
Cereals include sorghum, millet and wheat; oilseeds include sesame, groundnuts and sunflower; other crops include cotton, sugarcane, pulses and horticultural crops.

caveats: FAO's broad system areas describe national production context, not verified current cultivated or harvested area.
Crop selection must be tied to specific state, production system, water availability and season.
Conflict since April 2023 has disrupted irrigation infrastructure, field access, inputs and markets.

sections.topic: USDA FAS commodity production and harvested-area estimates
sections.source_name: USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Production – Sudan

observations.finding: Compared with 3.3 million tonnes in MY 2024/2025.
Compared with 793,000 tonnes in MY 2024/2025.
Compared with 1.68 million tonnes in MY 2024/2025.

caveats: USDA marketing-year estimates are an independent secondary cross-check and differ in period and methodology from the government-led CFSAM calendar-year harvest assessment.
Do not combine these production and area values with CFSAM totals without reconciling crop definitions, season, geographic coverage and marketing-year basis.
The displayed yield series requires crop-specific selection and metadata review before use.

sections.topic: market price, availability and trader monitoring
sections.source_name: IFPRI Sudan Essential Commodities Prices and Availability Monitor

observations.finding: Monitoring covers 18 states and 36 markets.
Data are collected fortnightly and aggregated monthly.
Dashboard reports prices in SDG per standard unit; the commodity-specific unit must be retained.
Monitoring covers prices, availability, quality and trader insights for food and agricultural commodities.

caveats: The dashboard describes a market-monitoring system; actual dated observations must be exported for each target commodity and market.
Market prices are not automatically farmgate producer prices.
Record market, state, commodity grade, unit, date and price source for every extracted observation.

sections.topic: 2026 commodity price movements, input costs and exchange rates
sections.source_name: IFPRI Sudan Market Prices and Availability Reports
sections.reference_date: July 2026 report published 4 August 2026; May 2026 report published 24 June 2026

observations.finding: Prices increased across most monitored food, livestock-product, agricultural-input, fuel and labour groups; availability generally declined, with pronounced regional disparities.
Darfur and Kordofan consistently recorded some of the highest food and fuel prices and lower commodity availability.
Traders reported rising parallel-market exchange rates, increasing input and fuel costs, supply-chain challenges and declining market availability.

caveats: The report summaries do not provide a complete farmgate price series or all commodity-level numeric values.
Retrieve the underlying monthly report tables and retain the source's official/parallel exchange-rate distinction.
Do not use a national market average as a substitute for a dated local producer price.

sections.topic: WFP monthly market prices and exchange-rate indicators
sections.source_name: WFP Logistics Cluster, Sudan Market Monitor – March 2026
sections.reference_date: March 2026 publication; underlying February 2026 market observations

observations.finding: Reported as 16.8 percent higher month-on-month and 103 percent higher year-on-year.

caveats: These are dated market-monitor values, not current exchange rates or farmgate prices.
The kantar weight must be verified from the original report's commodity/unit definition before any per-kg conversion.
Official and parallel exchange rates must remain separate and be time-stamped.

sections.topic: livestock population and pastoral production context
sections.source_name: FAO Sudan at a glance and 2025 CFSAM announcement
sections.reference_date: FAO country overview accessed 2026-11-01; CFSAM report announced 26 April 2026

observations.finding: FAO overview estimates about 115.4 million head.
Conflict damaged or looted veterinary infrastructure, suspended national vaccine production and reduced vaccination coverage.

caveats: These are broad population estimates and do not provide current state-level herd inventories or productive performance.
Livestock budgets require species, breed, herd structure, mortality, feed, water, veterinary, mobility and market transaction data.
Do not use a national livestock headcount as a yield, productivity or farm-profit assumption.

sections.topic: food security, conflict and agricultural operating risk
sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Sudan Country Brief and FAO 2025 CFSAM announcement
sections.reference_date: FAO GIEWS 24 September 2026; CFSAM announcement 26 April 2026

observations.item: Population facing IPC Phase 3 or worse
observations.finding: Over 40 percent of the analysed population was projected to face Crisis or worse acute food insecurity.

caveats: Conflict, displacement, field-access restrictions, damaged irrigation, input shortages, fuel prices and disrupted trade can make state-level averages unrepresentative.
Food-security indicators are not crop yield, production cost or farmgate-price observations.
Any future calculator recommendation must consider location-specific safety, access, rainfall and market connectivity.

sections.topic: 2026 rainfall and harvest risk, 2025 cereal baseline, USDA crop series and market monitoring
sections.source_name: FAO GIEWS Sudan Country Brief; USDA Foreign Agricultural Service Production – Sudan; IFPRI Sudan Essential Commodities Prices and Availability Monitor; FEWS NET Sudan September 2026–January 2027 update
sections.reference_date: FAO GIEWS 24 September 2026; USDA MY 2025/26 dataset accessed 4 November 2026; IFPRI August 2026 report; FEWS NET September 2026–January 2027 update

observations.item: National cereal production (sorghum, millet and wheat)
observations.finding: About 22 percent below 2024 and 19 percent below the previous five-year average. Aggregate total only; do not derive crop-specific yield or farm margins from it.
Rainfall deficit in a key sorghum-producing state; FAO Agricultural Stress Index indicated severe drought conditions over up to 55 percent of cropland.
Rainfall deficit in a key sorghum-producing state; FAO Agricultural Stress Index indicated severe drought conditions over up to 70 percent of cropland.
USDA series lists 2024/25 production at 3.3 million tonnes and 2025/26 at 3.0 million tonnes, down 9 percent; marketing-year estimate, not directly interchangeable with FAO calendar-year CFSAM.
USDA production page reports 6 million hectares. Retain source method and marketing-year definition; do not assume state-level distribution.
USDA series lists 2024/25 production at 793,000 tonnes and 2025/26 at 750,000 tonnes, down 5 percent.
USDA production page reports 2.5 million hectares; no state-level allocation adopted.
USDA lists oilseed peanut output at 1.0 million tonnes, down 41 percent from 1.68 million tonnes in 2024/25. This is oilseed commodity output, not a farmgate price or enterprise yield.
Domestic sorghum prices more than doubled on average in most monitored markets between January and August; August prices were more than twice their already elevated year-earlier levels.
Domestic millet prices increased on average by 77 percent over the period; August prices were 68 percent higher year-on-year.
National average diesel prices almost doubled and were more than twice the year-earlier level, increasing mechanisation, irrigation and transport cost risks.

Dashboard covers prices, availability, quality and trader insights, with commodity groups including cereals, vegetables, animal products, seeds, fertilisers, fuel and exchange rates. Dashboard metadata is not itself a dated transaction observation.

FEWS NET reports below- to severely below-average harvests across much of Greater Darfur and Greater Kordofan, with deteriorating pasture and water access, livestock distress sales and deaths in parts of North and West Darfur.

caveats: FAO calendar-year CFSAM totals and USDA marketing-year estimates use different periods and methodologies; retain them as separate series.
USDA crop production and harvested area are national estimates, not state-level yields or farm budgets. Verify selected commodity yield panels and definitions before using ratios.
FAO 2026 rainfall and crop stress assessments are seasonal risk evidence, not final harvest statistics.
IFPRI dashboard metadata confirms market monitoring coverage, but exported observations are still needed for exact market, date, commodity, unit and price values.
Market prices are not farmgate producer prices. Obtain producer-level evidence before setting calculator revenue assumptions.
Conflict and market access vary by state; no national average can represent inaccessible or severely disrupted production zones.

calculator_data_gaps: Obtain and extract the complete 2025 CFSAM tables by crop, state, planted/harvested area, production, yield and season.
Reconcile FAO calendar-year CFSAM totals with USDA marketing-year series; preserve methods, definitions and reporting periods.
Obtain state-level crop area and yield series for sorghum, millet, wheat, groundnut, sesame, cotton and other candidate crops.
Export dated IFPRI SPAMS observations from all accessible states/markets, preserving product, grade, SDG unit, date and market; distinguish market prices from farmgate producer prices.
Collect verified current farmgate producer prices by crop, state, season, quality and date.
Obtain current farmer-facing seed, fertiliser, crop-protection, labour, land preparation, machinery, irrigation, fuel, transport, storage and post-harvest quotations.
Build separate enterprise budgets for irrigated schemes, semi-mechanized rainfed farms and traditional rainfed systems.
Validate land access, water availability, rainfall and security at state/locality level before assigning production assumptions.
Obtain livestock purchase/sale prices, herd composition, feed, veterinary, vaccination, water, mortality and mobility costs by production system.
Document official and parallel SDG exchange-rate series with effective dates; never hard-code stale nominal prices.
safeguards: Research-only evidence; not a live calculator dataset.
Do not activate Sudan or change calculator formulas based on this file.
Do not treat national cereal production estimates as crop-specific yields or farm-level output.
Do not substitute retail/wholesale market prices for farmgate producer prices.
Do not combine CFSAM calendar-year harvest estimates and USDA marketing-year estimates without reconciling period, scope and method.
Preserve local units and currency/exchange-rate type with each price observation.
Do not generalize conflict-affected or drought-affected observations into normal-year enterprise assumptions.
Keep FAO calendar-year 2025 CFSAM cereal production separate from USDA marketing-year 2025/26 commodity estimates.
Do not infer representative crop yields by dividing national output by national harvested area without confirming matching crop definitions, period and methodology.
Do not use IFPRI dashboard metadata as a substitute for exported, dated market observations or farmgate producer prices.
Do not apply one national rainfall, conflict or access adjustment across Sudan.

notes: CFSAM state/scheme/sector tables report crop-specific cereal yield and production; do not collapse production systems into one yield.
Illustrative 2025/26 sorghum yield: Gedaref semi-mechanized 0.43 t/ha, traditional rainfed 0.43 t/ha; irrigated Aj Jazirah 2.68 t/ha. Different state/system records are not interchangeable.
National CFSAM crop-year and USDA marketing-year series differ in scope and timing; reconcile before using together.

market_evidence.note: WFP market-monitor price is a market observation, not validated farmgate producer price. Exchange rates are dated and channel-specific; do not use as current or universal conversion.

input_cost_evidence_gedaref_2025.note: Historical Gedaref reference prices from the CFSAM 2025 season; not national or current November 2026 quotes.

seasonal_risk_2026.note: FAO September 2026 brief; 2026 harvest outcome still pending at review date.

blockers: Obtain dated, commodity-specific farmgate producer prices by state/market, grade, unit and sale point; retail/market monitoring prices are not farmgate.
Extract and reconcile state-level CFSAM and USDA crop area, production and yield by crop, year and production system; do not mix crop-year and marketing-year series.
Refresh farmer-paid seed prices and seeding rates by crop/variety/state; 2025 Gedaref prices are reference-only.
Obtain current state-level fertilizer, crop-protection, labour, machinery, irrigation, water, fuel, transport, harvest and post-harvest cost schedules.
Build distinct enterprise budgets for irrigated, semi-mechanized rainfed and traditional rainfed systems and test each regional crop profile.
Account for conflict-related access constraints, 2026 rainfall deficits, currency instability and the November 2026 harvest uncertainty.
